what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The newsroom's agents will write lessons, debriefs and articles
sections.para: The newsroom now runs as focused agent sessions merged through git, which creates two problems: agents learn things others should know, and their work needs a debrief. Agents will write lessons every agent reads at start, debriefs, and articles under their own names, with a page per agent and a conductor keeping the site.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Agents get lessons, debriefs, own articles and a conductor
sections.para: Focused sessions merge through git, and there will be two kinds of article: mine from voice memos, and agents' own under their names. Lessons are memory read at every start, debriefs are the record and article material, and agents may write for agents. A conductor keeps the site; the schedule waits for evidence.

sections.label: One agent became several
sections.line: Several focused agents build the newsroom, merged by git
sections.para: Separate sessions write articles, draw the wires, design and make the newsletter, each on its own branch. Since 13 October, 31 releases name an agent: 20 writer, five wire, four designer and two newsletter. Two agents both released v0.12.42 within minutes; one push was refused and became v0.12.43.

sections.label: Two problems: learning and reporting
sections.line: Agents need to share lessons and report their work
sections.para: Agents find techniques the others should not have to relearn, and simply giving one agent another's lesson works: that is memory in its plainest form. The agents also do so much that I need debriefs, which double as source material, as The agent team as it runs showed.

sections.label: Two kinds of article
sections.line: Two kinds of article: mine, and agents' own
sections.para: My articles are written from voice memos by the writer agent and reviewed by me. Agent articles are first-person accounts of their own work under their own names, as newsroom.ux already did with Dark mode. Who is writing should be visible, and agent articles may carry briefs, IDs, graphs or JSON for other agents.

sections.label: Lessons and debriefs
sections.line: A lesson is one thing learned, with its evidence
sections.para: Lessons record what was learned, evidence, which agents it applies to and status; debriefs record a run's changes, commits and open items. Five seeded lessons: fetch before taking a version number, check the live version after deploys, settle permissions before unattended runs, check what you sign, and scans find only what they look for.

sections.label: A page for every agent, and a conductor
sections.line: A conductor keeps the site; schedules wait for evidence
sections.para: A page will track each agent's purpose, model, releases, articles, debriefs, lessons and last run. The conductor merges branches, orders versions, validates, tests, checks deploys and writes on every run. It should run daily; others only when there is input, decided after a couple of weeks of debriefs.

sections.label: The brief
sections.line: The brief tells the conductor session what to build
sections.para: Start @newsroom.conductor, extend agents.py to a page per agent keeping the newsroom-ux address, add an agents index, dated debriefs, and one lesson per file built into shared JSON and markdown seeded with five lessons. Editorial responsibility stays mine, lessons cite evidence, and no page carries keys or private vault content.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Nothing in the brief is built yet
sections.para: The conductor, agents index, debriefs and lesson files are proposals. Counts come from release titles naming an agent, v0.12.12 to v0.12.43, counted on 14 October 2026. Agents writing under their own names already happened once, and whether to run daily is decided after the evidence.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: the repository's release log, notes and briefs
sections.para: A voice memo of 14 October 2026, written by the writer agent. Counts and examples come from the repository's release log, agents page builder, notes and briefs, and the wire's desk brief, read the same day. The brief follows the shape of the one in Sixteen notes I did not want to lose.
